entry.title: From the Moon to the 50-Yard Line

media:group.media:title: From the Moon to the 50-Yard Line
media:group.media:description:
From the Moon to the 50-yard line.
Six months ago, NASA astronaut Christina Koch flew Philadelphia Eagles Super Bowl confetti around the Moon on the Artemis II mission. Yesterday, in a full circle moment, she served as honorary captain at an Eagles game, bringing a little Moon Joy to the field.
#ArtemisII #FlyEaglesFly #MoonJoy

media:group.media:title: 2026 Solar Eclipse @ 50,000 Feet
media:group.media:description:
These views, including footage from GoPro cameras, were captured by NASA's WB-57 aircraft during the 2026 total solar eclipse. Taking off from Iceland, our pilots studied the Sun's corona as they raced along the path of totality.
Credit: NASA

media:group.media:title: 2026 Total Solar Eclipse Over Spain
media:group.media:description:
On Aug. 12, 2026, a total solar eclipse passed over Greenland, Iceland, northern Russia, the Atlantic Ocean, Spain, and a small corner of Portugal.
Watch the moment that our teams captured totality over Spain.
Credit: NASA

media:group.media:title: NASA Moon Base Update (Aug. 4, 2026)
media:group.media:description:
Lunar landers, assemble!
In clean rooms across the country, commercial lunar landers are preparing for upcoming missions to the Moon.
From coast to coast, we're taking you behind the scenes to see the spacecraft that will deliver NASA instruments and help pave the way for humanity's first Moon Base.
Credit: NASA

entry.title: The Ultimate Away Game: World Cup Fever on the ISS 🌌🏆

media:group.media:title: The Ultimate Away Game: World Cup Fever on the ISS 🌌🏆
media:group.media:description:
World Cup fever just hit low Earth orbit!
Watch astronauts Jessica Meir, Sophie Adenot, Jack Hathaway and Christopher Williams take the beautiful game to the International Space Station in an epic microgravity match with the adidas FIFA World Cup Trionda Pro ball.
In addition to having fun with the Trionda, they also conducted experiments to analyze the ball's internal mass, which improves our understanding of how internal mass, including embedded sensors, can influence stability and rotation in real-world playing conditions. Just one more way space station science makes life better for people on Earth!
Credit: NASA Producer: Daniel Lauchu Music: Universal Production Music

entry.title: Get Unready With NASA's Artemis II Astronauts

media:group.media:title: Get Unready With NASA's Artemis II Astronauts
media:group.media:description:
When the Artemis II crew is “go” for slumber, a solid bedtime routine is essential. Their pre-sleep checklist helps ensure everything is set before lights out.
This video was recorded on April 9, 2026, during the eighth flight day of Artemis II's mission around the Moon.
Credit: NASA/Sonnet Apple

entry.title: Six Years of NASA's Mars Curiosity Rover

media:group.media:title: Six Years of NASA's Mars Curiosity Rover
media:group.media:description:
This time-lapse video tracks images taken by NASA's Curiosity Mars Rover between 2020 and 2026. These photos were used by Curiosity's science team to select rocks to study as the rover rolled its way across the Red Planet.
Learn more: https://go.nasa.gov/3QI7Npc

entry.title: Artemis II Watches Earth Set Behind the Moon

media:group.media:title: Artemis II Watches Earth Set Behind the Moon
media:group.media:description:
"Would you look at that, man!"
As Artemis II flew around the Moon on April 6, 2026, traveling further from Earth than any humans in history, mission commander Reid Wiseman captured this video of Earthset with his smartphone.
The sound you hear in the background is the shutter of mission specialist Christina Koch's camera as she captured photos of the moment. See more photos and videos from Artemis II: https://www.nasa.gov/artemis-ii-multimedia/
Credit: NASA

media:group.media:title: Reflections from the Artemis II Crew
media:group.media:description: "We've done this together. We took your hearts with us, and your hearts lifted our hearts." - Christina Koch⁣ ⁣ In a news conference held earlier today at NASA's Johnson Space Center, the Artemis II astronauts reflected on their test flight around the Moon.⁣ ⁣ Credit: NASA⁣ ⁣ #NASA #Artemis #Astronauts #Reflection

entry.title: Astronaut Victor Glover on Our Shared Spaceship: Earth

media:group.media:title: Astronaut Victor Glover on Our Shared Spaceship: Earth
media:group.media:description:
“You are special, in all of this emptiness. This is a whole bunch of nothing, this thing we call the universe. You have this oasis, this beautiful place that we get to exist together.”
In this video clip, Artemis II pilot Victor Glover reflects on our shared spaceship: Earth.

entry.title: The Artemis II Crew is Coming Home

media:group.media:title: The Artemis II Crew is Coming Home
media:group.media:description:
Homeward bound 🌎
Artemis II astronauts have flown around the Moon traveling 252,756 miles from Earth—farther than any other humans. They observed the lunar surface like never before, capturing iconic views.
Now, they’re coming home. The crew will splash down in the Pacific Ocean on Friday, April 10, around 8:07 p.m. EDT (0007 UTC April 11). Help us welcome them home: https://www.nasa.gov/ways-to-watch/

media:group.media:title: Artemis Daily Wrap: Flight Day 8
media:group.media:description: There's a lot to process on Day 8 of the @NASAArtemis II mission. With Earth in view from Orion's windows, the astronauts are packing up and reflecting on their lunar journey.

media:group.media:title: Artemis Daily Wrap: Flight Day 7
media:group.media:description: “You can see the surface of the Moon…we just went sci-fi.” On flight day seven, images from our @NASAArtemis II crew amazed, turning science fiction to science reality. From the lunar far side to a solar eclipse from the Moon, the views are EVERYTHING. No pressure to pick a favorite.

media:group.media:title: Artemis Daily Wrap: Flight Day 5
media:group.media:description: “On the Moon is a photo of my family. I pray it reminds you that we and America and all of the world are cheering you on.” Apollo 16 astronaut Charlie Duke recorded a special message for the Artemis II crew. Fitting that they hear encouraging words from the moonwalker as they close in on their lunar destination.

media:group.media:title: Full Capsule
media:group.media:description:
After successfully launching from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center on April 1, 2026, four astronauts are currently on their way to fly around the Moon on April 6 aboard the Orion spacecraft. The capsule has a habitable volume of 330 cubic feet, which is about the size of two minivans.
Credit: NASA
